Research framework

One decision workflow for civil and construction engineering

Bridge condition, hazard and network evidence from civil engineering flows through BridgeMind's generative AI core into construction decisions: scope, cost, schedule and recovery sequencing.

Civil engineering inputs

Condition and inspectionNBI ratings, age, material, span, load posting
Hazard exposureFlood, storm surge and hurricane scenarios
Network and trafficDetours, connectivity, emergency access
Community vulnerabilitySVI-weighted social consequence

BridgeMind AI core

Generative models turn engineering evidence into ranked, explainable options that engineers can inspect and challenge.

  • Risk-informed priority scoring
  • Closure and recovery scenarios
  • Plain-language rationale for each decision
  • Engineer-in-the-loop review

Construction engineering outputs

Rehabilitation scopeRepair, retrofit or replace, by method
Cost and schedulePhasing, work windows, budget trade-offs
Resources and logisticsCrews, equipment, materials, staging
Recovery sequencingWhich bridges reopen first after an event
Two lenses, same bridge

Ask the same question as an asset owner or a contractor

Switch lenses to see how BridgeMind frames a decision for planners and for delivery teams.

Which bridges carry the most risk?

Combines condition ratings, age and load posting into a transparent rehabilitation baseline across the 644-bridge inventory.

Output: tiered priority list

What breaks if one fails?

Tests closure effects on alternate routes, emergency access and travel time so each bridge is judged as part of the network.

Output: network consequence score

Who is affected most?

Weights hazard exposure by community vulnerability so recovery priorities reflect people, not only structures.

Output: equity-aware ranking

What work does each bridge need?

Translates condition evidence into candidate scopes (repair, strengthen or replace) so estimators start from a defensible baseline.

Output: scope options

How do we phase the work?

Balances cost, closure duration and traffic impact to propose staging and work windows that limit disruption.

Output: phased schedule logic

How fast can service resume?

Sequences post-disaster repairs by criticality and resource availability to shorten the path back to normal operations.

Output: recovery sequence

Bridge Intelligence

BridgeMind separates the structural baseline from live operations. The research layer provides risk context; the operational layer shows what is happening now.

01

Structural & Condition Context

Use NBI and inspection attributes such as condition ratings, age, material, span, load posting, and inspection evidence to build a transparent rehabilitation baseline.

02

Network Consequence

Combine traffic importance, alternate routes, connectivity, emergency access, and closure effects so the bridge is evaluated as part of the transportation network.

03

Hazard & Community Context

Bring flood and hurricane exposure together with community vulnerability so rehabilitation and recovery scenarios can account for more than asset condition alone.

Research baseline: The prototype uses the Miami-Dade analysis structure developed for BridgeMind, including a 644-bridge research inventory and 18 Tier 4 critical flags. These are research-layer values, not live agency status. Detailed RNI values and bridge-level rehabilitation history can be connected through the final validated research dataset.

About the Researcher & Concept

BridgeMind is presented as a research prototype built around a bridge rehabilitation and disaster-recovery research program.

Mostafa Sameer

Ph.D. Candidate · Moss School of Construction · Florida International University

Research interests represented in this concept include bridge rehabilitation prioritization, transportation network resilience, flood and disaster analysis, digital twins, data-driven risk assessment, and explainable AI for infrastructure management.

Data & Provenance

The website separates live operational feeds from research and inventory baselines so users can see which information is current and which information comes from the research dataset.

Florida 511 / FDOTOfficial Florida source for real-time traffic, incidents, congestion, closures, cameras, and travel information.fl511.com ↗
Miami-Dade DTPW GISAgency bridge layer used to display bridge geometries maintained by Miami-Dade Department of Transportation and Public Works.Bridge GIS layer ↗
FHP / FL511 ArcGIS feedPublic operational point layers used by this prototype for current roadway closures and congestion context.Operational layers ↗
NBI / Research BaselineStructural inventory and condition variables can be connected from NBI and the BridgeMind research dataset for validated rehabilitation scoring.NBI reference ↗
Important: Live operational data is provided by external public services and may be unavailable, delayed, or changed by the source agency. The disaster simulation numbers shown on this prototype are illustrative, not forecasts. BridgeMind is a research decision-support concept and does not replace inspection, design, emergency management, or engineering judgment.
